title: Wellington HF601 Memorial, Plage de Pors Liogan, Le Conquet
location_name: Plage de Pors Liogan, Le Conquet, Finistère, Brittany, France
cause_of_loss: Direct hit by coastal flak near Le Conquet at approximately 01:30. Aircraft crashed into the sea close to shore.
crew_summary: Five crew, all killed. Aircraft departed RAF Leconfield at 22:11 on 5 July 1943. Engaged by coastal flak near Le Conquet at approximately 01:30 on 6 July 1943. All bodies washed up on Pors Liogan beach and were buried with German military honours on 8 July 1943. One crew member (F/O Darbyshire) has no known grave and is commemorated on the Runnymede Memorial.
narrative:
Wellington HF601, coded HD-?, of 466 (RAAF) Squadron departed RAF Leconfield at 22:11 on the night of 5 July 1943, tasked with Operation Gardening — the RAF's codename for minelaying operations. HF601 was one of the Wellington crews detailed to seed sea mines in the Brest approaches, a strategically important channel used by German shipping off the Brittany coast.

The crew was a composite assembled from across 4 Group. Wing Commander Owen flew as pilot in command, attached to 466 Squadron from 4 Group Headquarters. The remaining four — Swain, Darbyshire, Long, and Ray — were attached from 196 Squadron. This mixing of experienced aircrew from different units was not unusual for operational minelaying sorties, where seniority and specific skill requirements could draw men temporarily from their parent squadrons.

Approaching the Brest peninsula in the early hours of 6 July, HF601 was caught by coastal anti-aircraft defences near Le Conquet — the westernmost point of the French mainland, at the entrance to the roadstead of Brest. A direct flak hit disabled the aircraft at approximately 01:30. HF601 crashed into the sea close to shore, killing all five men.

The bodies were recovered after washing up on Plage de Pors Liogan, a small beach in the commune of Le Conquet. Local French civilians and the German occupation authorities were responsible for their initial burial in the sand. On 8 July 1943 — two days after the crash — the five airmen were transported to the cemetery at Magueur/Lochrist and interred with German military honours, a practice observed in some occupied territories during this period.

Of the five men, four were subsequently identified and now rest in Le Conquet Communal Cemetery: Wing Commander Owen in individual Grave 4, and Flying Officers Swain, Pilot Officer Long, and Pilot Officer Ray together in Collective Grave 1–3. Flying Officer Frank Darbyshire, the bomb aimer, was never positively identified. He has no known grave and is commemorated on the Runnymede Memorial, Panel 124, alongside more than 20,000 aircrew of the RAF with no known grave.
memorial_address: Plage de Pors Liogan, Le Conquet, Finistère 29217, France
memorial_access_notes: Rural coastal location on the Pors Liogan beach, accessible on foot from Le Conquet. The beach is at the tip of the Crozon-area coastline near the westernmost point of France.
memorial_details: A stone memorial with plaque erected at Plage de Pors Liogan, the beach where the bodies of the crew were recovered in July 1943. The memorial stands in a rural coastal setting overlooking the sea. Erected in 1993 to mark the 50th anniversary of the crash. Inscription text unconfirmed from available sources.

crew.name: John Jervis Owen
crew.fate_detail: Killed when Wellington HF601 was shot down by coastal flak near Le Conquet. Body recovered from Pors Liogan beach and buried 8 July 1943 with German military honours.
crew.biography: Aged 35 at the time of his death, Owen held the rank of Wing Commander and was attached to 466 Squadron from 4 Group Headquarters for this operation. Son of John Alexander and Dora Sophia Owen; husband of Rosemary Valerie Owen of Feniton, Devon.

crew.name: Egbert Horace Swain
crew.fate_detail: Killed when Wellington HF601 was shot down by coastal flak near Le Conquet. Body recovered from Pors Liogan beach and buried 8 July 1943 with German military honours.
crew.burial_location: Le Conquet Communal Cemetery, Collective Grave 1-3
crew.biography: Aged 32. Attached to 466 Squadron from 196 Squadron for this operation.

crew.name: Frank Darbyshire
crew.fate_detail: Killed when Wellington HF601 was shot down by coastal flak near Le Conquet. No body was positively identified. Has no known grave.
crew.burial_location: No known grave. Commemorated on the Runnymede Memorial, Panel 124.
crew.biography: Aged 21 at the time of his death. Son of George and Nora Darbyshire of Wath, Ripon, Yorkshire. Attached to 466 Squadron from 196 Squadron. The only member of the crew without a known grave; commemorated on the Runnymede Memorial, Panel 124.

crew.biography: Aged 24. RCAF. Son of Albert James and Miriam Long of Prince Albert, Saskatchewan, Canada. Attached to 466 Squadron from 196 Squadron.
